name: PublishProof – Content QA & SafeFix
author: wazeplan

sections.description:
PublishProof is a free, self-contained content quality inspection tool for WordPress administrators. It checks saved post content and metadata and identifies items for human review before publication. All Free features work without an external account, API key, or payment.

Content inspections
* Review saved title, draft or published slug, featured-image assignment, and featured-image ALT.
* Find missing ALT attributes in stored IMG markup and review saved-source H1 counts.
* Check saved anchor destinations for malformed or placeholder URL values (not remote link availability).
* Show conservative potential CTA evidence and supported Rank Math / Yoast per-post override presence.
* Optionally request an HTTP response status for a published permalink on the site’s own host without following redirects. This does not validate rendering.

SafeFix: manual and reversible
* For eligible featured-image attachment ALT, manually write a description, confirm the shared Media Library impact, save, and re-inspect. One-step Undo is provided if unchanged.
* For supported anchors in saved HTML, manually approve editing exactly one href, re-inspect, and Undo the most recent change if unchanged. Payment/checkout destinations are protected.
* Inspect selected posts in read-only batches and optionally approve limited draft-image ALT proposals.
* Compare verified before/after finding counts and review a bounded per-administrator change history. This is not an immutable audit trail.

Reports and imported evidence
* Export the last individual inspection as JSON or a basic server-generated PDF, or print from your browser.
* Import separately created LiveProof browser evidence as JSON and export its evidence PDF. PublishProof does not run a browser, take screenshots, or upload your content to a cloud service.

PublishProof does not certify an entire website, verify outbound links, check purchases, render dynamic page builders, or execute checkout tests. It cannot guarantee accessibility, SEO rankings, security or legal compliance. Human review remains necessary.

Privacy

PublishProof runs its source inspections within your WordPress installation. No external AwesomePlan account or outbound SaaS data transfer is required. The optional published-permalink HTTP response check contacts your own site’s host only.

The plugin saves inspection results, limited inspection histories and verified change summaries to the current administrator’s WordPress user metadata. Undo snapshots can contain prior saved post HTML, link addresses and attachment ALT text. Manually imported LiveProof reports may include uploaded JPEG screenshots encoded in the current administrator’s metadata and their provided source URLs. These records are not published as public Media Library assets. The WordPress administrator controls which content is inspected or imported. Uninstalling the plugin removes its own stored user metadata, including Undo snapshots and imported evidence; it does not revert approved post or media edits or delete posts.
sections.installation:
1. Back up your WordPress site and database before activating a new plugin.
  2. Install PublishProof through Plugins > Add New, or upload the complete ap-publishproof ZIP.
  3. Activate and open Tools > PublishProof as a WordPress administrator.
  4. Choose an existing post, run an inspection, and review the findings. Scanning never edits post content.
  5. To use SafeFix, review the proposed change, select the explicit consent checkbox, and confirm. Re-inspect and use Undo if applicable.

Only users with the necessary WordPress capabilities can access the administrator interface. A supported link edit also requires unfiltered_html and post-edit permission.
sections.faq:
Does PublishProof require a paid account?

No. This free plugin works locally in WordPress without an AwesomePlan account or API key.

Does a PASS mean the live page is error-free?

No. Results are scoped to stored HTML and metadata. Themes, page builders and dynamic blocks can change the rendered page. A PASS means only that the named check passed within its documented scope.

Does it check broken external links or actual payment buttons?

No. Saved URL syntax is not an outbound reachability check, and payment and purchase workflows are not inspected.

Will it change posts automatically?

No. Scans are read-only. SafeFix writes require an authenticated administrator, post or media permissions, a fresh saved-content fingerprint, a WordPress nonce, and explicit approval. WordPress hooks may run when content is saved.

Why is Korean text different in the PDF?

The built-in PDF renderer is currently English/Latin-first. Use the JSON export to preserve Unicode, including Korean.

Can it take screenshots?

Not on its own. The LiveProof tab can import screenshots and findings captured separately by a compatible browser worker. Imported evidence is not independently verified by this plugin.
sections.changelog:
0.3.3

  • Reworked the Saved Links URL sanitizer to use the WordPress-recognized esc_url_raw() directly after wp_unslash(); nonce, eligibility and protected destination checks are unchanged.
  • The release ZIP contains no staging-only markdown files; when patching an existing installation, delete any previously left DEPLOY_README_KO.md file from the plugin root.

0.3.1

  • Clarified and strengthened sanitization for approved ALT, link, batch selection and LiveProof JSON import inputs.
  • Made read-only admin URL parameters explicit and documented why nonce tokens are required for state-changing POST actions, not navigation.
  • No changes to licensing, billing, cloud services, saved-content inspection rules, or consent/Undo safeguards.

0.3.0

  • Initial public Free release candidate based on the M3.1 staging-tested core.
  • Source-only editorial inspections, manual SafeFix ALT and saved-link editing with Undo, history, PDF/JSON export and manual imported LiveProof evidence.
  • Consolidated release metadata and privacy documentation; kept all Free functionality local to WordPress.
  • Clarified report scope and removed staging-only text from the interface.
